mutations.because: the acquire-window recovery itself. With it dropped, a TERM delivered while the acquire child runs leaves the lock behind naming a pid that is about to be gone: the signal is deferred until that foreground child exits and the child is NOT signalled, so it finishes its rename and writes the slot it won, and LOCK_HELD is still 0 when the deferred exit 143 runs, which means release_lock had nothing to give back. The name survives until some later acquire judges it abandoned - a leak, not a permanent hold. This fails on EVERY shell in the list rather than on one of them, because the deferral is POSIX and not a quirk of a particular /bin/sh: the test signs the parent pid only, and parks that child inside the existing CF_GATE_TEST_PAUSE_BEFORE_MV hook (inherited by the acquire child) so the window is deterministic instead of a race. Measured against the unfixed script before the lane started: exit 143 with no release line and a cf-gate.lock left naming the dead gate, 1 run in 1, under both dash and bash.
